scope: Disposition of every entry in the 0.4 draft changelog as retrieved on 9 November 2026 (upstream commit b2569c5). Planned names the work item in the upgrade plan that implements it; Done records implementation with the stated evidence and limits. A newer 0.4 snapshot changes this list.

changes.notes: chooseSignInType already tries Direct, then Device, then Mediated. Still to do: the 0.4 validator profile warns when a Company that offers sign-in offers Device but not Direct (F7).

F1 chooses a version from poppy.json and supported_versions; F2 sends Poppy-Version on every Session request; R1 retries once after version_unsupported; M1 gives the mock linked documents and version checks; F7 validates them. Kit: discovery.supported-versions, discovery.versions-same-company, session.version-missing, session.version-unsupported.
F1 reads each extension as a list of versions; F2 sends Poppy-Extensions, fixed per Session, and drops extensions from the client metadata; M1 takes the declaration from the header.
F5 stores the versions each conversation started in; C6 handles version_mismatch by finishing in a Session with those versions or starting a new conversation.
W1 requests the scope only from a Company that lists browser_session_endpoint and falls back on insufficient_scope; the mock requires it; F7 checks scopes_supported.
W2 reads it before requesting the scope. Kit: discovery.web-unscoped.
W2: a Personal Agent SHOULD NOT browse such a Company. Kit: discovery.web-disabled.

F5 migrates the conversation rows, index and protocol-log trigger; C1 reads working, handoff, closed and responder; U1 to U3 update the tools, Activity and protocol log. Kit: conversations.closed-not-working, conversations.working-settles.

changes.change: Requests are accepted, then acted on
changes.notes: C2: a POST without wait returns only conversation_id; read until working is false; send the next request only after acceptance when order matters.

changes.change: Request IDs on every conversation request
changes.notes: F5 stores request IDs durably for messages, handoff, cancel and close; C2 sends a top-level id. Kit: conversations.missing-request-id, conversations.invalid-request-id, conversations.request-id-boundaries, conversations.request-id-conflict, conversations.request-id-other-conversation, conversations.request-id-other-url.
C3 adds handoff cancel and direct_conversation_open; U1 adds a model tool. Kit: conversations.cancel-without-handoff, conversations.closed-handoff-cancel.

changes.change: What a message took into account
changes.notes: C5: as_of_cursor only on messages with author.type agent; as_of_request read as a hint.
C4: close returns 202; the row stays open until closed is true; read until working is false before closing.

T1 reads tasks.endpoint per Session with the Session header and no token, and takes feedback.endpoint from it; T2 feeds the skill index to the Skills milestone. Kit: tasks.response, tasks.alternative-references, tasks.skill-index.

Adopted (decision 43). W3 surfaces Poppy-Operation from the agent's own browser, approves at the operations endpoint, repeats the browser's request with its own replay safety, and keeps the local form-consent card. Needs A1.
K1: the mock answers refresh with invalid_grant and revocation with success. No agent change: it already refuses sign-in with auth.disabled.

changes.change: Client assertions when no tokens exist
changes.notes: K1: the mock may skip assertion checks while it has issued no refresh token.

changes.change: `extension_required` in a JSON body at APIs
changes.notes: openapi-dispatch.ts already reads a JSON body; X1 moves the mock's apis.ts to a body and keeps the WWW-Authenticate reading for 0.3 only.

changes.change: Device sign-in links on the issuer or Company domain
changes.notes: K3 applies to the 0.4 profile only: under 0.3 a multi-domain issuer may legally put its device page on another protected resource's host, and refusing it ends the sign-in.

changes.change: Refresh token lifetimes left to the Company
changes.notes: No agent change. The mock's refreshTokenTtl only sets an expiry at issue, so nothing depends on a fixed lifetime.

changes.change: A DPoP key per User ID
changes.notes: H1 keys DPoP keys by issuer and User ID. Today it holds only because each issuer has one User ID. Can ship on 0.3.

H2 uses derived metadata only when its resource is the derived identifier, and, per decision 43, requires the same exact match for metadata from a resource_metadata hint; fixes MCP's root-metadata fallback in mcp-transport.ts. Can ship on 0.3.
K2: describeScopes prefers an OpenAPI description today, the 0.3 order; 0.4 prefers auth.scopes.

changes.change: One User ID per delegated key at the Company
changes.notes: The agent already makes one delegated key per User ID (5.2). K1 lets the mock reject a key reused for another User ID.

changes.change: Sessions found by User ID too
changes.notes: K1 keys mock Sessions by client_id, sid and User ID, keeping the violation for an agent that changes sub or agent_id within a Session. No change on the wire.
O1: a revision may keep its number when only summary changes.

changes.change: Operations: new terms for the same action
changes.notes: O1: review how the terms card presents a new revision for the same operation_id.
A1, per decision 43: approvals bind to the agent, User ID and account, not one sid; signed-out stays separate from signed-in.

changes.change: When and how the User approved
changes.notes: O1 sends approved_at (Unix seconds; an Integer in the header) and input_type without personal or device data; the mock parses Integer members.

changes.change: Operations: what counts as the same request
changes.notes: O1: the agent already repeats the same request; the mock compares requests by meaning, and the agent may approve an earlier revision.
The client signing keys are Worker secrets, apart from sealed refresh tokens. Rotating DPoP keys at refresh is optional; H1 keeps one per User ID.
Company guidance. The agent side, approving earlier terms the User prefers, is part of O1.
Feedback goes only to feedback.endpoint through poppy_feedback; under 0.4 that endpoint comes from the tasks response (T1).
Company guidance for clients other than Personal Agents.
